questions.stem: Factor the given rational function and state its decomposition:
questions.explanation: The numerator is a difference of squares, which factors to (x + 2)(x - 2). Since (x + 2) is in both the numerator and denominator, it can be cancelled out, leaving x(x - 2)/(x + 2).
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Cancelling out (x - 2) instead of (x + 2). This would lead to an incorrect decomposition.

questions.stem: Factor the given rational function and state its decomposition:
questions.explanation: The numerator factors to 3x(x - 2), and the denominator is a difference of squares, which factors to (x + 3)(x - 3). The common factor of 3 can be factored out from the numerator.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Factoring the denominator incorrectly as (x - 3)^2. This would lead to an incorrect decomposition.

questions.stem: Factor the given rational function and state its decomposition:
questions.explanation: The numerator factors to 4x^2(3x - 2), and the denominator factors to 2x(3x - 2). The common factor of (3x - 2) can be cancelled out, leaving 4x(x - 1)/(2x).
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Cancelling out x instead of (3x - 2). This would lead to an incorrect decomposition.

questions.stem: Factor the given rational function and state its decomposition:
